recipes.name: Bourbon Whiskey BBQ Sauce
ingredients_raw: 0.33333334326744 teaspoon hot pepper sauce, or to taste

steps.text: Combine bourbon, garlic, and onion in a large skillet over medium heat; simmer until onion is translucent, about 10 minutes.

Stir in ketchup, brown sugar, vinegar, tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce, liquid smoke, salt, black pepper, and hot pepper sauce; bring to a boil, reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer for 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Bourbon Whiskey BBQ Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This smoky bourbon BBQ sauce has generous amounts of bourbon whiskey, brown sugar, ketchup, and garlic. The ribs won't know what hit them!

review.reviewBody: Update: I figure out this tastes the same no matter which bourbon whiskey I use. I now pick up one of the cheapest bottles they have and it's great. Original: This deserves more than 5 stars! I made this for Memorial Day BBQ and it was wonderful! Used Maker's Mark and didn't change the recipe other than adding a bit more hot sauce. Cooked it outside on the grill on Saturday for Monday's BBQ. I strained the onions out and I wish I would have followed some other suggestions of cutting the onions into wedges to make it easier, but it all worked out in the end. Letting the chicken soak in the BBQ sauce for 24 hours from yesterday until today made it even better!

I’ve been on the hunt for a really good homemade sauce. I read dozens of the reviews on this sauce before I decided to jump on the bandwagon. Admittedly, I like a lot of different styles or barbecue and sauce and this didn’t disappoint. I found that it had great elements to it... sweet, tangy, spicy, smoky... all beautifully melded together!

So here we go... I didn’t change a thing when it came to the ingredients, I followed that part to a T! After reading a review about using a crock pot, I decided to go that route. Chopped up my onion, threw everything in and gave it a good stir. Set to high, stirred a few times over a few hours and OMG did the house smells incredible. I do use a good bourbons in my cooking because I don’t believe in adding bourbon or wine to my dishes that I wouldn’t drink, so Angels Envy tends to be my preferred cooking bourbon and again, it didn’t disappoint. 

I do like a little texture in my barbecue sauce, so I used an immersion blender to smooth it out and it worked beautifully... I highly recommend that step to anyone, whether they like a smooth or bodied sauce. I let it sit in the crock to cook for an hour or so before I transferred it to a jar and it’s just a dark, beautifully rich color. 

I made it a day in advance... I currently have a 9# pork butt in an apple cider brine that I’ll be throwing on the smoker in the morning.... planning on dropping off some dinner to friends tomorrow night and I’m confident this sauce will be a hit wit

Added 1/2 a minced orange bell pepper, a couple of large slices of Mezzetta roasted red peppers and followed remaining instructions, with the exception of running through a strainer. Instead, used my emulsion blender until smooth. Let flavors meld in refrigerator over night and then made 3 racks of baby backs on the Traeger smoker! Yum!

This is a fantastic sauce, I did use my vita mix after the simmering was done to really incorporate the onions and garlic then I thinned it back down with a little apple juice and it was amazing, the best I’ve ever made.

It's a great recipe. I've made it multiple times in large batches. I made it again recently, but took one reviewers suggestion to add 1 Tbsp molasses (I used black strap) to the recepie to add depth of flavor and body. THIS WAS THE TRICK that sent it over the top. It made the sauce more savory and less tomato-y. It perfected the sauce for me.

A family favorite, instead of the mincing and frying of the onion and garlic I put it through the magic bullet and leave it all in. I cut the sugar in half and use our favorite Canadian Rye. I quadruple the recipe and section it out in the freezer. Been making this for years.
Awesome! I made and used habenaro bourbon. 1 C and 1 C water. Wonderful levels of flavor. I canned small jars for use as Christmas presents. Great recipe!

This is a very good BBQ sauce. I loved everything about it except for one thing. 2 cups of ketchup is too much for the ratio of other ingredients. 1 cup ketchup and 1 cup tomato puree is my solution to this. Otherwise the ketchup takes over. I made this for a large event just as set out, and needed to do last minute emergency fix because the ketchup took over. Nice recipe after the making the adjustment.

Great recipe! I added only about 1/3 cup of coconut sugar and that’s sweet enough for us! Makes a lot - we’ve used it on one batch of ribs, then roasted chicken. Will make ribs again in a few days to use it up. Excellent- highly recommend!

So easy and really tasty! Only change, I used 3 Tbl. dried onion flakes to keep from having to strain it. Worked perfectly! 
 I put it over shredded, cooked chicken and served on toasted buns with cole slaw. Plenty left for other dishes.

Great sauce with just a few of my notes: I rounded the whiskey up to a full cup and rather than finely mincing the onion or garlic for the browning process I rough chopped both and puréed the simmering sauce (instead of straining) for maximum flavor.
I added some jalapenos and a habanero!
I lived this sauce! Tangy, not too sweet. The only thing I did different was use honey bourbon instead of regular.

I wouldn't change a thing! I've made this barbecue sauce for at least 3 years now and I get asked for the recipe every time. My family and friends love it on ribs, chicken, and pulled pork. I have used a variety of bourbon and even Jack Daniel's Tennessee Honey, which I also love.
I make this and can it ..the whole family loves it
I think next time I'll use garlic powder and onion powder instead of the onion and garlic, that way I wont have to strain it out but everything else is great about the recipe.
Wow, this sauce is awesome! This is my go to bbq sauce recipe. I switch up liquid smoke flavors, hickory, mesquite and applewood. Other than that, recipe is great as is.
Awesome. Excellent rib sauce.
I've made this sauce just about every year to pair with a brisket. It is always a favorite and gets lots of compliments.

The liquid smoke is a necessity. I added 1/4 cup of Pineapple juice too. I used Maggi sauce instead of Worcestershire sauce. I left out the tomato paste. For heat I added Smoked paprika and sweet Chilli flakes. It is awesome!
